messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 pager — multi-GPU collective errors on cluster 'inference-prod-usw2'. Symptoms: repeated NCCL WARN and communicator reset, CUDA errors (illegal memory access / 700), several runtime containers repeatedly OOM/killed. Affected model shard: gpt-large-v2 (tp8). Impact: ~30% of requests failing with 5xx; latency spikes. Paging oncall SRE.

Alice (oncall): ack — looking. Starting triage. Which pods/nodes are flapping?

Raj: seeing a lot of NCCL logs like: `NCCL WARN Call to commAbort - aborted` and `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in pod logs. I pulled logs from pod/gpt-large-v2-0: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference logs pod/gpt-large-v2-0 -c runtime | tail -n 120
# sample
[2026-03-15 04:21:12] NCCL WARN Call to commAbort, rank 2
[2026-03-15 04:21:12] cuda driver error 700: Illegal address
[2026-03-15 04:21:13] runtime: failed to allocate workspace, OOM
[2026-03-15 04:21:13] container restarted by OOM killer
```

Mei: nodes implicated: gw-node-12, gw-node-13, gw-node-21. Looks like a hardware or driver-level memory fault intermittently causing one worker to die and NCCL to deadlock the collective. We should avoid full-scale restarts until we can fail traffic off those nodes.

Dino (runtime): immediate mitigation checklist I've used before:
- cordon + drain the suspect nodes so they don't accept new shards
- restart `nvidia-containerd` / container runtime on drained nodes
- enable `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` for the runtime subprocess to reduce collective hard-fail behavior
- if IB seems flaky, set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (force sockets) for a short window to see if it stabilizes

Commands: 
```bash
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gw-node-12 gw-node-13 --ignore-daemonsets
kubectl drain gw-node-12 gw-node-13 --delete-emptydir-data --force --ignore-daemonsets -n inference

# restart runtime on node (via SSH/runbook)
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-containerd
# or on k8s node containerd restart
sudo systemctl restart containerd

# rollout with env tweak (temporary):
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-runtime NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_DEBUG=INFO --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime
```

Alice (oncall): executing cordon/drain for gw-node-12 and gw-node-13 now. Shifting traffic to us-east fallback pool (route policy). I'll monitor error rate.

(5m later)
Alice (oncall): drained gw-node-12/13. Restarting runtime on those hosts now. Error rate dropped from 31% -> 12% after draining. Still seeing occasional resets from gw-node-21.

Raj: I pushed temporary route policy to redirect new sessions away from tp8 shard group and fallback to tp4 shards for non-critical tenants. That reduced customer errors for top 3 tenants. Leaving sticky sessions unaffected.

Dino (runtime): FYI logs after restart show driver recovery messages on gw-node-12: 
```
[  954.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  954.124000] nvidia: CPU: 1 PID: 18234: kernel reports GPU reset
```
This indicates a GPU reset. Could be hardware/driver instability. Recommend we: continue draining gw-node-21 and open a hardware ticket for gw-node-12.

Mei: Confirmed. I've created a temporary capacity bump on Dedicated pool to absorb traffic while we take nodes offline. Also triggered alert to Support to notify affected customers (top 5 B2B customers) with ETA remediation.

Eng Runtime: adding to thread — we'll collect heap dumps / coredumps from the crashed runtime containers for postmortem. Please preserve `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, kernel dmesg and `journalctl -u nvidia-containerd`.

Alice (oncall): action summary for owners: 
- SRE (Alice/Raj): continue cordon/drain gw-node-21, monitor errors, ensure all tp8 shards removed from live routing.
- Runtime (Dino/Eng Runtime): collect coredumps, set NCCL env flags (async handling + debug), check driver version differences.
- Platform/Infra (Mei): open hardware ticket for gw-node-12, schedule node replacement if HBA/PCI errors persist.
- Support: customer notifications sent, working on compensating credits for impacted tenants.

Raj: quick patch applied: `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` rolled out as a short-lived config, rollback plan in 30m if we see regressions. Also set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` for the vulnerable shards as an experiment.

(10m later)
Alice (oncall): error rate stabilized to ~3% after all mitigations. No new crashes in last 12 minutes. We're keeping gw-node-21 cordoned pending hardware investigation. Customer impact has been reduced to low severity.

Dino (runtime): collected logs and uploaded tarball to infra-artifacts: `s3://redwood-incidents/2156789012/gw-node-12-logs.tar.gz`. Added coredumps and `nvidia-smi` output.

Mei: hardware ticket created with vendor — ticket RED-7890. ETA for onsite diag: 48h.

Alice (oncall): handing off to Mei for next shift. Handoff note: mitigations applied (cordon/drain gw-node-12/13/21; NCCL env toggles; traffic reroute to tp4 fallbacks; logs & coredumps collected; vendor ticket opened). Current state: service healthy with residual low error rate (~3%), capacity buffer increased. Please monitor for recurrence and start postmortem timeline.

Mei: ack — taking oncall. I'll keep watches on the dashboard and follow up with runtime/infra for next steps. Scheduling postmortem meeting for 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.

Alice (oncall): thanks — created incident record and assigned owners. We'll produce RCA + action items after hardware confirmation. :white_check_mark:
